headline: S&P closes at record high as soft jobs report eases rate-hike concerns
summary: The S&P 500 closed at a record high after US nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 jobs in July, below estimates, according to the Labor Department. The softer data eased rate-hike concerns.
why: The S&P 500 is the benchmark index of about 500 large US-listed companies, and its level reflects broad investor sentiment toward the US economy. Payroll data shapes expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate policy.
why_moved: Nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, below forecasts, which reduced concern that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates.
